claim: The original held-out fixed-point pilot did not show uniformly beneficial related-source pretraining.
independent_units: Two paired units (17,42); sample sizes and A/B/C share their unit's inputs/initialization.
protocol_scope: n=10; 188-token legacy evaluator; one target; 64/256/1024 target samples; fixed 800 adaptation updates.
support: The raw two-seed sample-size curves retain negative and near-zero average gains.
limitations: One target and two seeds; a negative average does not mean every seed is negative. Fixed update budget causes unequal reuse as sample count changes.
suggested_paper_use: Motivation and exploratory sample-size appendix; not a general sample-efficiency law.

claim: Development selection and the historical doubled source budget did not remove mean negative transfer.
independent_units: Same two historical units 17/42; no new independent repeats.
protocol_scope: fixed_points, 256 samples; equal three-LR adaptation searches; new isolated test; source 2400 versus 4800 steps.
quantitative_anchor: Development-selected 2400: B-A=-17.26 pp, C-A=-8.74 pp, B-C=-8.52 pp; 4800: B-A=-10.55 pp, C-A=-12.87 pp, B-C=+2.32 pp.
support: Failure to load/reset weights is not supported by engineering audits; negative means persist under the selected protocol.
limitations: Historical continuation uses low terminal LR and is not the fresh relative-budget comparison in task-count v2; reused development inputs and hypothesis remain exploratory.
suggested_paper_use: Protocol diagnostic; distinguish clearly from task-count v2's budget intervention.

claim: The nominally matched candidate pair differed markedly in learnability under multitask training.
independent_units: Two paired source-model units; source records within units are not independent experiments.
protocol_scope: anti_fixed_points versus successions, identical n=10 source inputs and 25% example shares.
quantitative_anchor: Mean source development accuracy at 2400: 77.98% versus 45.12%; at 4800: 89.31% versus 51.86%; source-histogram TV 0.0443/0.0520.
support: Similar marginal answer distributions do not ensure similar learning curves.
limitations: These are mixture-learning differences, not intrinsic difficulty or a causal isolation of relation effects.

claim: Transfer varies across held-out targets, and the candidate replacement contrast changes sign across seeds for all four targets.
independent_units: Three paired units 17/42/73; first two fixed-point units reuse historical training; four targets are not 12 independent repeats.
protocol_scope: Four targets, 256 samples; four sources; 4800 source steps; equal three-LR development selection; new tests.
quantitative_anchor: Mean B-A: fixed_points -10.12 pp; exceedances +2.59 pp; left_to_right_minima -1.53 pp; longest_decreasing_run +11.20 pp. B-C signs are mixed for all four targets.
support: The fixed-point negative effect is not a universal outcome across the tested mathematical targets.
limitations: LDR A/C are near majority; eligibility at 8192 single-task examples does not establish learnability at 256. All tested direct candidate relations have identity answer maps.
suggested_paper_use: Main broad-target exploratory panel; retain all four targets.

claim: Single-task and mixture references show both degradation and improvement, with exposure confounding.
independent_units: Three units; 84 deduplicated seed-task-model-state records share inputs/tasks and are not 84 independent repeats.
protocol_scope: Single-task 4800 and mixture 4800 share total updates, but single-task exposure is four times larger; single-task 1200 matches exposure only.
quantitative_anchor: 84 deduplicated source records: 60 declines >=5 pp, 6 improvements >=5 pp, 18 smaller gaps; successions seed 73 improvement +43.55 pp retained.
support: Composition accompanies different source learning; low performance cannot be summarized only by relatedness labels.
limitations: The references do not isolate interference or synergy because exposure, alternation and LR histories differ.

claim: The same candidate-source replacement has different observed effects across background sets.
independent_units: Three paired blocks 17/42/73; reuse from v3; 42 unique selected models, not 54 independent display rows.
protocol_scope: Two targets selected from v3, three backgrounds, 256 samples; fixed source candidates and paired slots.
quantitative_anchor: FP deficiencies-v3 interaction +4.36 pp (seeds +1.42,+0.34,+11.33); LDR recoils-v3 -12.00 pp (seeds -20.07,+2.00,-17.92).
support: Observed background-dependent variation motivated the two frozen v5 hypotheses.
limitations: Case/background selection is exploratory; v3/v4 reused units must not be counted as independent replications. Must present v5 follow-up beside these effects.

claim: The prespecified positive fixed-point background interaction did not reproduce in mean direction.
independent_units: Five new paired units 101/211/307/401/503; old three exploratory units are not pooled.
protocol_scope: Primary difference (B-C)_deficiencies-(B-C)_original, n=10, 256 samples, frozen budget and selection.
quantitative_anchor: Mean -3.02 pp, SD 15.75; 2/5 direction matches; 95% paired-t CI [-22.57,+16.54]; two-contrast simultaneous CI [-27.63,+21.60].
support: The exploration's positive replacement interaction is not corroborated by the new point estimate.
limitations: Wide intervals include both directions; failure of directional replication is not proof of zero background effect. Five units and finite-pool dependence limit interval interpretation.

claim: The LDR confirmation point estimate matches the exploratory direction but does not establish a stable interaction.
independent_units: Five new paired units, shared across targets; not 10 independent target replicates.
protocol_scope: Primary difference (B-C)_recoils-(B-C)_original with a two-contrast interval family.
quantitative_anchor: Mean -13.15 pp, SD 12.67; 4/5 direction matches; 95% CI [-28.89,+2.58]; simultaneous CI [-32.97,+6.66].
support: A large negative point estimate remains uncertain under the prespecified paired analysis.
limitations: Both interval types include zero; LDR A 53.56% and recoils B/C 53.50%/52.38% are near 53.67% majority. No claim of reliable universal background dependence.
suggested_paper_use: Mandatory uncertainty alongside v5 fixed-point non-replication.

claim: Same-input joint derivability and transformed-input joint derivability are distinct design facts.
independent_units: Deterministic mathematical audits, not learning replicates.
protocol_scope: Position partition and inverse identity; four-source scalar query models audited for 12 v4 groups.
quantitative_anchor: fixed_points+exceedances+deficiencies=n; exceedances(p)=deficiencies(p^-1). All 12 same-input groups have counterexamples; 7/12 groups recover targets under 32 transformed queries, and five have insufficiency witnesses.
support: Both B/C fixed-point deficiencies groups can recover FP from D(p),D(p^-1), but the position partition alone cannot recover FP from one D label.
limitations: Valid relations are not instance leakage; no explicit paired-query training or mechanism demonstration was performed. Counterexamples restrict only the declared query model.

claim: The unified platform distinguishes endpoints, canonical templates, instances and encoding variants.
independent_units: Deterministic registry inventory, not statistical replicates.
protocol_scope: Legacy unary/binary interfaces remain callable; the canonical dataset is unary only.
quantitative_anchor: 48 legacy + 6 new = 54 endpoints; 48 canonical mathematical templates; 62 declared instances; 56 materialized unary non-alias instances; one input encoding.
support: Machine-readable definitions, parameters, ranges, complexities, encoding and relation status are available under one interface.
limitations: 48 templates are not 48 mathematically independent capabilities; binary pools are not generated or certified by this release.
suggested_paper_use: Primary resource contribution with explicit counting conventions.

claim: The three focus families provide differentiated tasks while explicitly retaining constants and aliases.
independent_units: Deterministic function classes under named relations.
protocol_scope: Cycle decomposition, global subsequences and permutation blocks at n=8/10/12 and default parameters.
quantitative_anchor: Focus: 16 templates / 24 instances; 22 nonconstant instances; 23 same-input classes; 20 registered answer-preserving transformation classes (19 nonconstant).
support: Cycle family: 6 templates / 8 instances; subsequences: 5/9; blocks: 5/7. I1=D1=n constants remain visible.
limitations: Other lengths/parameters can be degenerate; known transformation classes do not classify arbitrary answer maps or all joint relations.
suggested_paper_use: Resource counts and protection against count inflation.

claim: Exact generators have independent algorithm checks and explicit relation evidence.
independent_units: 6105 deterministic fixtures, not 6105 training or statistical units.
protocol_scope: Exhaustive S1...S7 plus 192 larger-n fixtures; historical v5 certificates reused.
quantitative_anchor: 272741 independent label comparisons; 445581 new formula/bound pointwise checks; 45 new relations + 29 historical relations reused; zero historical formula rechecks.
support: Independent cycle, subsequence, RSK and block algorithms verify oracle implementation; proof and finite-check status remain separate.
limitations: Finite verification is not a general proof; mathematical correctness does not imply model learnability.

claim: The versioned sequence protocol supports large and structured answers without silent truncation.
independent_units: Engineering and data audits, not statistical replicates.
protocol_scope: permworld_sequence_v1, one_line_v1, current 203-token vocabulary; 188 legacy IDs retained.
quantitative_anchor: 9216 fixed objects / 516096 exact labels; n=30,k=15 integer 155117520 round trip; 32 canonical I3 labels >=100; all focus instances fit a 128-token context.
support: Delimited base-100 integers and nested lists are explicitly encoded; oversized legacy examples are visibly rejected.
limitations: The six scalar representatives do not calibrate structured-output learning; legacy and platform accuracies use different protocols.

claim: Six frozen single-task representatives span sharply different attainable learning levels under one budget.
independent_units: Two paired seed/data units 617/829; six tasks sharing this protocol are not 12 independent replicates.
protocol_scope: 2400 updates/task; n=8/10/12 all trained; complete-answer-plus-EOS development accuracy; no inference on reserved tests.
quantitative_anchor: Mean endpoint development: cycle_count 42.84%; longest_cycle 22.53%; LIS 86.26%; I3 count 25.26%; components 99.74%; largest_component 99.02%.
support: All six retained; block majority is 77.08%, so high accuracy needs baseline context; cycle_count at n=12 has development accuracy 35.74% versus 36.72% majority.
limitations: Development only: no unseen-length extrapolation, transfer or entire-family ranking; 12 runs are six tasks x two units.
suggested_paper_use: Single-task resource calibration panel, explicitly labeled development.

claim: At 4M tokens, the tested count curves do not show universally monotonic transfer improvement.
independent_units: Three new paired units 1103/2207/3301; chains, targets and shared baselines are not extra replicates.
protocol_scope: Two fixed nested chains; k=2/4/8/16; four targets; 256 samples; n=10/12; full answer plus EOS.
quantitative_anchor: 24 pretrained models / 108 target fits; LIS k16-k2 mean -5.47 pp alpha / -6.02 pp beta, negative in all three repeats of each chain; all eight cycle-count means are at or below A.
support: LIS retains positive mean gains over A while losing benefit as k increases; modest component gains and fixed-point chain/seed variation are preserved.
limitations: Changing k changes source composition, relations and exposure; three paired units cannot establish a pure task-count causal effect or scaling law.
suggested_paper_use: Finite task-count results across all four targets.

claim: The fixed-point average peak is unstable, and many source endpoints remain underlearned.
independent_units: Three paired units; 180 source-task/model records are not 180 independent replicates.
protocol_scope: Development-selected primary checkpoint; fixed 4M budget; no result-triggered extension.
quantitative_anchor: FP alpha-k8 gains +26.17,+12.01,-10.94 pp (mean +9.08, SD 18.73); 61/180 source endpoints are at or below their training-derived majority baseline.
support: The mean peak is not a stable optimum; limited source learning motivates a frozen budget follow-up.
limitations: Selecting the best k after inspecting outcomes would overstate this exploration; source-accuracy/transfer association does not establish a mechanism.
suggested_paper_use: Retained negative and uncertain evidence beside the count curve.

claim: A larger relative-progress budget reverses the LIS count disadvantage in alpha and reduces it in beta.
independent_units: Three new paired units 4103/5207/6301; two chains share these units, not six independent interactions.
protocol_scope: Primary LIS; fixed chain composition at each k; 2x2 comparison of k=2/16 and 4M/32M; fresh paired initialization; 256 samples.
quantitative_anchor: Alpha D4=-6.18 pp, D32=+11.75, interaction +17.94 (SD 7.89); beta D4=-5.79, D32=+0.75, interaction +6.54 (SD 5.96); both interactions are positive in all three repeats.
support: The direction of k16-k2 depends on budget in the prespecified alpha case; beta shrinks the disadvantage without positive D32 in all three repeats.
limitations: The hypothesis comes from v1, with limited new repeats and composition coverage; different absolute-token LR paths mean budget and trajectory are not separately identified.
suggested_paper_use: Primary fixed-composition budget interaction, conditional on the tested design rather than universal.

claim: The auxiliary fixed-point budget interaction has opposite signs across source chains.
independent_units: Three new paired units, shared with LIS; the auxiliary target does not double the independent repeat count.
protocol_scope: Same 2x2 protocol; fixed_points is the auxiliary target.
quantitative_anchor: Alpha interaction +41.41 pp (SD 3.27), beta -9.08 (SD 11.55); alpha-k16-32M test accuracy 88.44%, +23.63 pp over A; beta-k16-32M 43.39%, -21.42 pp over A.
support: A larger budget does not generally eliminate negative transfer; seven of eight fixed-point conditions retain negative mean gains.
limitations: Relation availability and improved source learning do not prove formula use; the auxiliary outcome must not replace the primary LIS question.
suggested_paper_use: Auxiliary counterexample to universal budget benefits.

claim: The budget comparison increases repeated training on a fixed pool, with audited pairing and budget-specific LR paths.
independent_units: 24 source models and 54 target fits across three repeat units; not 78 independent repetitions.
protocol_scope: 12 fresh-initialization budget pairs; the same 8192 source objects per unit; uniform example shares; whole-example token stopping.
quantitative_anchor: 431999672 actual pretraining tokens; 82944000 adaptation tokens; 12 pairs verified; 135 formal checkpoints checked; 54 development selections; 324 test CSV rows; zero new test forwards in the audit.
support: 32M extends the sampled-example prefix but starts from random weights, not 4M weights; per-task coverage and repeated exposure counts are explicit.
limitations: Eightfold total tokens are not eightfold independent data or strict per-task exposure matching; absolute learning rates differ from the first update.
suggested_paper_use: Reproducibility and qualification of causal scope.
